added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(P_\lambda\) and \(Q_\lambda\) be probability laws dominated by \(\nu\), indexed by \(\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k)\), and let \(\mathcal Z=\bigcup_{j=1}^k\mathcal Z_j\) be a measurable partition.  Suppose \(P_\lambda(\mathcal Z_j)=Q_\lambda(\mathcal Z_j)=p_j\), and that the conditional laws on \(\mathcal Z_j\) depend only on \(\lambda_j\), with the two families differing only for \(j\in S\).  For a prior \(\varpi\), write \(\bar p=\int p_\lambda\,d\varpi(\lambda)\) and \(\bar q=\int q_\lambda\,d\varpi(\lambda)\), and define
\[
 \delta_1=\max_{j\in S}\sup_\lambda\int_{\mathcal Z_j}
 \frac{(p_\lambda-\bar p)^2}{p_\lambda p_j}\,d\nu,
 \quad
 \delta_2=\max_{j\in S}\sup_\lambda\int_{\mathcal Z_j}
 \frac{(q_\lambda-p_\lambda)^2}{p_\lambda p_j}\,d\nu,
\]
\[
 \delta_3=\max_{j\in S}\sup_\lambda\int_{\mathcal Z_j}
 \frac{(\bar q-\bar p)^2}{p_\lambda p_j}\,d\nu.
\]
If \(\bar p/p_\lambda\le b<\infty\) and \(np_j\max(1,\delta_1,\delta_2)\le b\) for every \(j\), then, for a constant \(C_b\) depending only on \(b\),
\[
 H^2\!\left(\int P_\lambda^{\otimes n}\,d\varpi(\lambda),
              \int Q_\lambda^{\otimes n}\,d\varpi(\lambda)\right)
 \le C_b n\left(\sum_{j\in S}p_j\right)
 \left[n\left(\max_{j\in S}p_j\right)
       (\delta_1\delta_2+\delta_2^2)+\delta_3\right],
\]
where \(H^2(P,Q)=\int(\sqrt{dP}-\sqrt{dQ})^2\).

upstream.citation: James M. Robins, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen, Lingling Li, and Aad W. van der Vaart. Semiparametric minimax rates. Electronic Journal of Statistics 3:1305--1321, 2009.

attestation.note: Checked against the published author manuscript at PMC11960818, Section 3.2, Lemma 2; the displayed statement transcribes the hypotheses, three delta quantities, and Hellinger conclusion used here.

added_lemmas.justification: This is the published localized partition-mixture Hellinger inequality instantiated in the sign-conditioned comparison.
added_lemmas.gap: The present exact-uniform overlapping-bump construction still requires a new local refinement and density calculation, supplied by the proved adaptation below.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(0<h<H\leq1\) such that \(H^{-1}\) and \(H/h\) are positive integers and each macro cube of side \(H\) contains at least four fine cubes of side \(h\).  Fix bounded smooth functions \((B_j)\) and \((G_Q)\) with bounded overlap such that \(G_Q=\sum_{j\subset Q}B_j^2\), \(0\leq G_Q\leq1\), and, for constants \(1\leq C_b<\infty\) and \(c_b>0\) depending only on the fixed bump shapes and \(d\),
\[
 \left[\sum_j a_jB_j\right]_s\leq C_bh^{-s}\max_j|a_j|,
 \qquad
 \left[\sum_Q z_QG_Q\right]_s\leq C_bH^{-s}\max_Q|z_Q|
 \tag{1}
\]
for \(s\in\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\}\), together with the analogous supremum bounds.  Assume that every fine cube contains a core of volume at least \(c_bh^d\) on which only its own bump is active and is bounded below by \(c_b\), and that each \(G_Q\) is a translated and rescaled copy of one nonconstant macro bump \(g\).  Let the macro signs \((\sigma_Q)\) be independent Rademacher variables.  For each fine coordinate \(j\subset Q\), put \(U_j=q_e\varepsilon_j\), \(V_j=q_b\eta_j\), where \(q_e,q_b>0\), \(0<\delta\leq q_eq_b\), and \(\vartheta=\delta/(q_eq_b)\).  Conditional on the macro signs, take the fine pairs independently with
\[
 \mathbb P_1(\varepsilon_j=a,\eta_j=b)=\frac14,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P_0(\varepsilon_j=a,\eta_j=b\mid\sigma_Q)
 =\frac14\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\},
 \quad a,b\in\{-1,1\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Writing \(u=\sum_jU_jB_j\), \(v=\sum_jV_jB_j\), and \(G=\sum_Q\sigma_QG_Q\), define every null component by
\[
 e_0=\frac12+u,
 \qquad m_{0,0}=\frac38+v,
 \qquad \tau_0\equiv\frac18,
 \tag{3}
\]
and every alternative component by
\[
 e_1=\frac12+u,
 \qquad m_{0,1}=\frac38+v-2\delta G,
 \qquad \tau_1=\frac18+4\delta G.
 \tag{4}
\]
Impose the construction-side inequalities
\[
 C_bq_eh^{-\alpha}\leq L,
 \quad C_b\{q_bh^{-\beta}+2\delta H^{-\beta}\}\leq L,
 \quad 4C_b\delta H^{-\gamma}\leq L,
 \quad C_bq_e\leq\frac14,
 \quad C_bq_b+2\delta\leq\frac18.
 \tag{5}
\]
Then all four masses in (2) are nonnegative, all coordinate means vanish, \(U_j^2=q_e^2\), \(V_j^2=q_b^2\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_0(U_jV_j\mid\sigma_Q)-\mathbb E_1(U_jV_j)
 =\delta\sigma_Q.
 \tag{6}
\]
Every law induced by (3)--(4) belongs to \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), every null component has exactly constant CATE, and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the bumps and \(d\), satisfy
\[
 c\delta\leq D(P_1)\leq C\delta
 \tag{7}
\]
for every alternative component.  The null and alternative prior-predictive laws match for one observation conditional on all macro signs and also for observations in distinct active fine coordinates.  For observations \(1,2\) in the core of one fine cube and observation \(3\) in the core of a distinct fine cube of the same macro cube, define
\[
 \xi_i=s_e(A_i)B_i,
 \qquad \upsilon_i=s_b(A_i,Y_i)B_i,
 \qquad \kappa_i=\xi_i\upsilon_i,
\]
where
\[
 s_e(a)=2(2a-1),
 \qquad
 s_b(a,y)=\begin{cases}
 -8/5,&(a,y)=(0,0),\\
 8/3,&(a,y)=(0,1),\\
 -2,&(a,y)=(1,0),\\
 2,&(a,y)=(1,1).
 \end{cases}
\]
The exact third canonical projection of the null-minus-alternative prior-predictive likelihood ratio is
\[
 \delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3,
 \qquad
 \mathcal L_{12}
 =(\xi_1+\xi_2)(\upsilon_1+\upsilon_2)
 -(1+q_e^2\xi_1\xi_2)(\kappa_1+\kappa_2),
 \tag{8}
\]
and it is not identically zero.  Its contribution to the squared \(L^2(P_\star^{\otimes n})\) norm is at least
\[
 c(n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4.
 \tag{9}
\]
At \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), choose legal integer resolutions satisfying \(h\asymp\delta^5\), \(H\asymp\delta\), and put \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\) for fixed \(0<\epsilon\leq1\).  Then \(n^2h\delta^4\), \(n^3hH\delta^4\), and \(n^4h^2H\delta^4\) are, respectively, \(o(1)\), \(\Theta(\epsilon^{10})=O(\epsilon^4)\), and \(o(1)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because \(0\leq\vartheta\leq1\), every mass in (2) is nonnegative, and their sum is one because \(\sum_{a,b}ab=0\).  Direct summation gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_0(\varepsilon_j\mid\sigma_Q)
 &=\frac14\sum_{a,b}a\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\}=0,\\
 \mathbb E_0(\eta_j\mid\sigma_Q)
 &=\frac14\sum_{a,b}b\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\}=0,\\
 \mathbb E_0(\varepsilon_j\eta_j\mid\sigma_Q)
 &=\frac14\sum_{a,b}ab\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\}
 =\vartheta\sigma_Q.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{10}
\]
Under \(\mathbb P_1\), all three expectations are zero.  Since \(\varepsilon_j^2=\eta_j^2=1\), multiplication of (10) by \(q_e\), \(q_b\), and \(q_eq_b\), respectively, proves (6) and the asserted square identities.

We verify every class condition.  The synthesis bounds in (1) and the first three inequalities in (5) give
\[
 [e_k]_{\alpha}\leq L,
 \qquad [m_{0,k}]_{\beta}\leq L,
 \qquad [\tau_k]_{\gamma}\leq L,
 \quad k\in\{0,1\},
\]
where the constant \(\tau_0\) has seminorm zero.  The corresponding supremum synthesis bounds give
\[
 |u(x)|\leq C_bq_e,
 \qquad |v(x)|\leq C_bq_b,
 \qquad |G(x)|\leq1.
 \tag{11}
\]
The last two inequalities in (5) therefore imply
\[
 \frac14\leq e_k\leq\frac34,
 \qquad
 \frac14\leq m_{0,k}\leq\frac34,
 \qquad
 \frac14\leq m_{0,k}+\tau_k\leq\frac34,
 \quad k\in\{0,1\}.
 \tag{12}
\]
Indeed, under the null \(m_{0,0}\in[1/4,1/2]\) and \(m_{0,0}+\tau_0\in[3/8,5/8]\); under the alternative both \(m_{0,1}=3/8+v-2\delta G\) and \(m_{0,1}+\tau_1=1/2+v+2\delta G\) obey (12).  Since all these functions are bounded by one, their Hölder-ball supremum restrictions follow from \(L\geq2\).

For each displayed triple of regressions, take \(X\) exactly uniform on the full cube, draw \(A\mid X\) as Bernoulli with mean \(e_k(X)\), draw binary \(Y(0),Y(1)\) conditionally independently of \(A\) given \(X\), with means \(m_{0,k}(X)\) and \(m_{0,k}(X)+\tau_k(X)\), and set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  The probabilities exist by (12); this construction gives consistency and conditional exchangeability.  Thus the design, smoothness, margin, consistency, and exchangeability assumptions defining \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\) all hold.  Equation (3) gives \(\tau_0\equiv1/8\) component by component.

Let \(M=H^{-d}\), let \(g_Q\) be the rescaling of \(g\) to \(Q\), and put \(\mu_r=\int_{[0,1]^d}g(x)^r\,dx\).  Disjoint macro supports and a change of variables give
\[
 \int G^2\,d\lambda=\mu_2,
 \qquad
 \int G\,d\lambda=H^d\mu_1\sum_Q\sigma_Q.
 \tag{13}
\]
Since \(H^dM=1\), the square of the second quantity is at most \(\mu_1^2\).  The fixed \(g\) is nonconstant, so strict Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(\mu_2-\mu_1^2>0\).  Equations (4), (13), and the definition of \(D\) yield
\[
 4\delta(\mu_2-\mu_1^2)^{1/2}
 \leq D(P_1)\leq4\delta\mu_2^{1/2},
 \tag{14}
\]
which proves (7).  The bump requirements are realizable as follows.  Choose a nonnegative smooth macro collar \(w_Q\), supported in \(Q\), that is positive on an inner cube, and set \(g_Q=w_Q^2\).  On the fine lattice choose fixed translates \((\varphi_j)\) with bounded overlap and with \(\sum_j\varphi_j^2\) bounded below on the support of \(w_Q\).  Put \(p_j=\varphi_j/(\sum_k\varphi_k^2)^{1/2}\) there and \(B_j=w_Qp_j\), extending by zero across the collar.  Then \(\sum_{j\subset Q}B_j^2=g_Q\).  The fixed templates can be chosen with a core on which one \(p_j\) equals one and the others vanish.  Rescaling the templates gives (1), the fixed overlap bound, and the required core volumes.

Relative to the interior reference law with conditional cell probabilities
\[
 (p^\star_{00},p^\star_{01},p^\star_{10},p^\star_{11})
 =\left(\frac5{16},\frac3{16},\frac14,\frac14\right),
 \tag{15}
\]
direct multiplication of the four Bernoulli cells gives
\[
 L_{0,i}=(1+s_e(A_i)u_i)(1+s_b(A_i,Y_i)v_i)
 \tag{16}
\]
and
\[
 L_{1,i}=(1+s_e(A_i)u_i)
 \{1+s_b(A_i,Y_i)v_i+s_e(A_i)s_b(A_i,Y_i)\delta\sigma_QG_Q(X_i)\}.
 \tag{17}
\]
These are exact identities.  Conditional independence of fine coefficient pairs and (6) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_0(u_iv_i\mid\sigma)=\delta\sigma_QG_Q(X_i),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_1(u_iv_i\mid\sigma)=0.
\]
All linear coefficient means vanish, and expansion of (16)--(17) therefore gives the common conditional one-observation predictive likelihood
\[
 \mathbb E_0(L_{0,i}\mid\sigma)
 =\mathbb E_1(L_{1,i}\mid\sigma)
 =1+s_e(A_i)s_b(A_i,Y_i)\delta\sigma_QG_Q(X_i).
 \tag{18}
\]
If observations involve disjoint active fine-coordinate sets, conditional independence makes both joint predictive likelihoods the product of the factors in (18).

Now put observations \(1,2\) in the core of one fine coordinate, observation \(3\) in a distinct fine core in the same macro cube, and write \(r=\delta\sigma_Q\).  On these cores,
\[
 L_{0,i}=(1+\xi_iU_j)(1+\upsilon_iV_j),
 \qquad
 L_{1,i}=(1+\xi_iU_j)(1+\upsilon_iV_j+\kappa_ir).
\]
For the repeated coordinate, (10) and the fixed squares yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 N_{12}:={}&\mathbb E_0(L_{0,1}L_{0,2}\mid\sigma)\\
 ={}&1+\xi_1\xi_2q_e^2+\upsilon_1\upsilon_2q_b^2
 +(\xi_1+\xi_2)(\upsilon_1+\upsilon_2)r
 +\xi_1\xi_2\upsilon_1\upsilon_2q_e^2q_b^2,
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{19}
\]
whereas
\[
 A_{12}:=\mathbb E_1(L_{1,1}L_{1,2}\mid\sigma)
 =(1+\xi_1\xi_2q_e^2)
 \{(1+\kappa_1r)(1+\kappa_2r)+\upsilon_1\upsilon_2q_b^2\}.
 \tag{20}
\]
Consequently
\[
 N_{12}-A_{12}=r\mathcal L_{12}-r^2\mathcal Q_{12},
 \qquad
 \mathcal Q_{12}=\kappa_1\kappa_2(1+q_e^2\xi_1\xi_2).
 \tag{21}
\]
Multiplication by the common singleton factor \(1+\kappa_3r\), averaging over the Rademacher sign, and Möbius subtraction of the one- and two-coordinate marginals gives exactly \(\delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\).

This projection is nonzero.  If all three binary rows equal \((1,1)\), then
\[
 \mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3
 =32B_1B_2B_3^2\{1-2q_e^2(B_1^2+B_2^2)\}.
 \tag{22}
\]
Because \(C_b\geq1\), (5) implies \(q_e\leq1/4\), so the last factor is at least \(3/4\).  The event has fixed positive probability under (15), and the selected cores each have volume at least \(c_bh^d\).  There are, up to fixed constants,
\[
 H^{-d}(H/h)^d\{(H/h)^d-1\}\asymp H^dh^{-2d}
\]
ordered choices of a repeated and a distinct singleton fine coordinate in one macro cube.  Integrating the square of (8) over the cores gives a one-triple squared norm at least \(ch^dH^d\delta^4\).  Canonical kernels on different sample-coordinate triples are orthogonal under \(P_\star^{\otimes n}\), because a coordinate in their symmetric difference integrates to zero.  Summation proves (9).

Finally take \(d=\gamma=1\) and \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\).  Choose integer meshes within fixed factors of \(h=C_h\delta^5\) and \(H=C_H\delta\), where the fixed constants \(C_h,C_H\) are large enough, put \(q_e=q_b=2\delta^{1/2}\), and then take \(\epsilon\) small and \(n\) large.  Every inequality in (5), including the corrected two margin inequalities, then holds; moreover \(\vartheta=1/4\).  For \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), direct substitution gives
\[
 n^2h\delta^4\asymp\epsilon^9n^{-7/10}=o(1),
 \qquad
 n^3hH\delta^4\asymp\epsilon^{10}=O(\epsilon^4),
 \qquad
 n^4h^2H\delta^4\asymp\epsilon^{15}n^{-1/2}=o(1).
\]
This proves all assertions with the mechanically correct synthesis margins.
added_lemmas.justification: This replaces the mechanically invalid unit-synthesis margin by the actual bounded-overlap synthesis margin and rechecks every class condition.
added_lemmas.gap: It is a construction diagnostic, not an all-regime converse.
added_lemmas.consumer: The corrected fifth-projection diagnostic and the sign-conditioned Hellinger lower bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under the hypotheses and notation of \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection-corrected}\), put observations \(1,2\) in the core of one fine cube and observations \(3,4,5\) in the cores of three mutually distinct fine cubes, all four fine cubes lying in the same macro cube.  The exact fifth canonical projection of the null-minus-alternative prior-predictive likelihood ratio is
\[
 \delta^4\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5.
 \tag{23}
\]
It is not identically zero, and its contribution to the squared \(L^2(P_\star^{\otimes n})\) norm is at least
\[
 c(n)_5h^dH^{3d}\delta^8.
 \tag{24}
\]
At \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h\asymp\delta^5\), \(H\asymp\delta\), and \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\) with fixed \(\epsilon>0\), the right side of (24) has order \(\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\) and diverges.  Hence this four-atom construction cannot have a support-controlled squared-likelihood connected remainder of order \(O(\epsilon^4)\) at the proposed \(n^{-3/10}\) separation.  This conclusion concerns that fixed-reference \(L^2\) comparison and does not rule out a sign-conditioned Hellinger comparison using the common predictive marginal.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For \(S\subseteq\{3,4,5\}\), equation (21) in \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection-corrected}\) and conditional independence across distinct fine coordinates give
\[
 F_{12,S}=\mathbb E_{\sigma_Q}\left[
 (r\mathcal L_{12}-r^2\mathcal Q_{12})
 \prod_{i\in S}(1+\kappa_ir)\right],
 \qquad r=\delta\sigma_Q.
\]
Every marginal difference omitting observation \(1\) or \(2\) is zero.  The fifth canonical projection is therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{S\subseteq\{3,4,5\}}(-1)^{3-|S|}F_{12,S}
 &=\mathbb E_{\sigma_Q}\left[
 (r\mathcal L_{12}-r^2\mathcal Q_{12})
 \prod_{i=3}^5\{(1+\kappa_ir)-1\}\right]\\
 &=\mathbb E_{\sigma_Q}\left[
 r^4\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5
 -r^5\mathcal Q_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5\right]\\
 &=\delta^4\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5,
 \end{aligned}
\]
because the macro sign is Rademacher.  This proves (23).

If all five binary rows equal \((1,1)\), then
\[
 \mathcal L_{12}=8B_1B_2\{1-2q_e^2(B_1^2+B_2^2)\},
 \qquad \kappa_i=4B_i^2.
\]
As \(C_b\geq1\), the corrected hypothesis \(C_bq_e\leq1/4\) implies \(q_e\leq1/4\), so the expression in braces is at least \(3/4\).  On the bump cores the displayed product is bounded away from zero.  The binary event has fixed positive reference probability.  The number of ordered choices of the repeated fine cube and three distinct singleton cubes in one macro cube is
\[
 H^{-d}(H/h)^d\{(H/h)^d-1\}\{(H/h)^d-2\}\{(H/h)^d-3\}
 \asymp H^{3d}h^{-4d}.
\]
Integration over the five cores contributes \(h^{5d}\), so the squared norm of the fifth canonical kernel is at least \(ch^dH^{3d}\delta^8\).  Orthogonality across distinct five-element sample-coordinate subsets and summation over those subsets prove (24).  At the stress scaling,
\[
 (n)_5hH^3\delta^8\asymp n^5\delta^{16}
 =\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The asserted fixed-reference conclusion follows.
added_lemmas.justification: This preserves the exact fixed-reference fifth-projection diagnostic under the corrected synthesis margins.
added_lemmas.gap: Its divergent squared-likelihood norm is specific to expansion around the fixed interior reference.
added_lemmas.consumer: The complete-frontier question retains it as a warning against fixed-reference chi-square proofs.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under the corrected four-atom construction at \(d=\gamma=1\) and \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), choose a locally finite smooth squared partition with a fixed overlap multiplicity, set \(q_e=q_b=2\delta^{1/2}\), and take integer meshes \(h\asymp\delta^5\) and \(H\asymp\delta\).  Let \(\bar P_{0,\sigma}^{(n)}\) and \(\bar P_{1,\sigma}^{(n)}\) be the null and alternative prior-predictive laws conditional on all macro signs, and let \(\bar P_k^{(n)}=\int\bar P_{k,\sigma}^{(n)}\,d\Pi(\sigma)\).  There are constants \(C<\infty\), \(\epsilon_0>0\), and \(n_0(\epsilon)\), depending only on the fixed bumps and \(L\), such that, for \(0<\epsilon\leq\epsilon_0\), \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), and \(n\geq n_0(\epsilon)\),
\[
 H^2(\bar P_0^{(n)},\bar P_1^{(n)})
 \leq Cn^2h\delta^2
 \leq C\{n^2h\delta^4+n^3hH\delta^4+n^4h^2H\delta^4\}
 \leq C\epsilon^{10}.
 \tag{25}
\]
The first upper bound is the additional term left by conditioning and Hellinger convexity.  It equals \(O(\epsilon^7n^{-1/10})\), so it is negligible at this scaling, although it is not uniformly dominated by the right side of (25) for arbitrary unrelated \((n,h,H,\delta)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix the macro signs.  By equation (18) of \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection-corrected}\), the null and alternative one-observation predictive densities, relative to the interior reference law, coincide and equal
\[
 \bar \ell_\sigma(x,a,y)
 =1+s_e(a)s_b(a,y)\delta\sigma_{Q(x)}G_{Q(x)}(x).
 \tag{26}
\]
The score product has absolute value at most \(16/3\).  Since \(0\leq G_Q\leq1\) and \(\delta\leq1/64\),
\[
 \frac{11}{12}\leq\bar\ell_\sigma\leq\frac{13}{12}.
 \tag{27}
\]
Thus every Radon--Nikodym denominator below is bounded away from zero.  Equivalently, the original margins imply that each conditional binary cell probability in every component is at least \(1/16\); hence the ratio of the common marginal density to any component density is at most \(9\).

Partition the covariate line into intervals \((R_r)\) of lengths at most a fixed multiple of \(h\), refining the supports of the locally finite squared partition.  On each \(R_r\), at most \(K_0<\infty\) fine-coordinate pairs are active.  Couple, independently over fine coordinates, a draw from the correlated null four-atom law and a draw from the independent alternative four-atom law.  Exact uniform design gives
\[
 p_r=P(X\in R_r)=\lambda(R_r),
 \qquad \max_rp_r\leq C_0h,
 \qquad \sum_rp_r=1.
 \tag{28}
\]

Write \(p_\lambda\) for a null component density and \(q_\lambda\) for the coupled alternative component density, conditional on the fixed macro signs.  The amplitude choices, the fixed overlap multiplicity, and the synthesis bounds give, pointwise on \(R_r\),
\[
 |p_\lambda-\bar p_\sigma|
 \leq C_1\delta^{1/2},
 \qquad
 |q_\lambda-p_\lambda|
 \leq C_1\delta^{1/2},
 \tag{29}
\]
where the densities are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure times counting measure and the constant uses only the fixed cell probabilities and bumps.  To verify (29) directly, expand (16)--(17): every term that varies with a fine atom contains at least one of \(u\) or \(v\), whose absolute values are bounded by \(C_bq_e\) and \(C_bq_b\), and all remaining factors are bounded by (12); the deterministic macro adjustment is \(O(\delta)\).  Since every component cell probability is at least \(1/16\), squaring (29), summing over the four binary cells, integrating over \(R_r\), and dividing by \(p_r\) yields
\[
 \delta_1\leq C_2\delta,
 \qquad \delta_2\leq C_2\delta.
 \tag{30}
\]
Equation (26) gives \(\bar p_\sigma=\bar q_\sigma\), so \(\delta_3=0\).  Equations (27)--(28) also give \(\bar p_\sigma/p_\lambda\leq9\) and, because \(nh\asymp n\delta^5=\epsilon^5n^{-1/2}\),
\[
 np_r\max(1,\delta_1,\delta_2)\leq9
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), after enlarging the harmless fixed constant in the cited lemma.

Equations (28)--(30) fully instantiate the numerical part of \(\texttt{lem:kbrw-partition-mixture-hellinger}\).  A literal application to the intervals \(R_r\), however, would be invalid: on a smooth transition interval one observation depends on the atoms attached to two adjacent fine coordinates, so the lemma's coordinate-locality premise is not satisfied by declaring duplicated local parameters.  We now prove the required bounded-overlap extension directly.

Fix \(X_1=x_1,\ldots,X_n=x_n\).  Let \(N(i)\) be the set of fine coordinates whose bumps are nonzero at \(x_i\), and join \(i\) and \(j\) when \(N(i)\cap N(j)\neq\varnothing\).  Conditional on the macro signs, the fine-coordinate atoms are independent.  Hence the null and alternative predictive laws of the binary observations factor over the connected components of this graph.  A singleton component has the same law under both priors by (26).

Consider a connected component \(C\) of size \(k\geq2\).  Expand the exact component likelihoods (16)--(17).  Under the independent alternative atom law, a moment \(\mathbb E_1(U^aV^b)\) vanishes unless both \(a\) and \(b\) are even.  Under the correlated null atom law,
\[
 \mathbb E_0(U^aV^b\mid\sigma_Q)-\mathbb E_1(U^aV^b)
 =\begin{cases}
 \vartheta\sigma_Qq_e^aq_b^b,&a\text{ and }b\text{ are odd},\\
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{31}
\]
When it is nonzero, the absolute value in (31) is at most \(\vartheta q_eq_b=\delta\), because \(q_e,q_b\leq1\).  Every term introduced by the deterministic alternative adjustment contains a factor \(\delta G\).  Thus every monomial in the difference of the two \(k\)-observation predictive cell probabilities contains a factor of absolute value at most \(\delta\).  Each observation contributes only a fixed number of bounded score and bump factors, because the overlap multiplicity is \(K_0\).  Therefore, for every binary cell and fixed covariates,
\[
 |r_{0,C}-r_{1,C}|\leq C_3^k\delta.
 \tag{32}
\]
The original margins give \(r_{1,C}\geq16^{-k}\), and there are \(4^k\) binary cells.  Consequently
\[
 H^2(r_{0,C},r_{1,C})
 \leq\chi^2(r_{0,C},r_{1,C})
 \leq C_4^k\delta^2.
 \tag{33}
\]
For product laws, \(H^2(\bigotimes_C R_{0,C},\bigotimes_C R_{1,C})\leq\sum_CH^2(R_{0,C},R_{1,C})\), because the Hellinger affinities multiply and \(1-\prod_Ca_C\leq\sum_C(1-a_C)\) for \(0\leq a_C\leq1\).

It remains to average (33) over the exact uniform design.  Local support and fixed overlap imply that adjacent observations in the graph have covariates at distance at most \(C_5h\).  For a specified set of \(k\) sample indices to be connected, one of its at most \(k^{k-2}\) labeled spanning trees must have every edge this short; the tree count follows by the injective Pr\"ufer deletion code into the \(k^{k-2}\) sequences of length \(k-2\).  Conditioning successively along a rooted tree and using uniform design gives probability at most \((C_6h)^{k-1}\).  Hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_X\sum_{C:\,|C|\geq2}C_4^{|C|}\delta^2
 &\leq\delta^2\sum_{k=2}^n\binom nk C_4^k k^{k-2}(C_6h)^{k-1}\\
 &\leq C_7n^2h\delta^2\sum_{k=2}^n(C_8nh)^{k-2}
 \leq C_9n^2h\delta^2.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{34}
\]
For the second inequality, \(\binom nk\leq n^k/k!\) and \(k^{k-2}/k!\leq e^k\); the latter follows from \(\sum_{j=1}^k\log j\geq\int_1^k\log x\,dx=k\log k-k+1\).  The last inequality uses \(nh\asymp\epsilon^5n^{-1/2}\to0\).  Since the law of \(X^n\) is the same under both predictives, (33)--(34) prove, uniformly in the macro signs,
\[
 H^2(\bar P_{0,\sigma}^{(n)},\bar P_{1,\sigma}^{(n)})
 \leq Cn^2h\delta^2.
 \tag{35}
\]
Squared Hellinger distance is jointly convex: pointwise Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\(\sqrt{(\int p_\sigma d\Pi)(\int q_\sigma d\Pi)}
\geq\int\sqrt{p_\sigma q_\sigma}\,d\Pi\), and integration proves the claim.  Averaging (35) over the common outer-sign prior therefore proves the first inequality in (25), with no further term.

At the prescribed scaling,
\[
 n^2h\delta^2\asymp\epsilon^7n^{-1/10},
 \quad
 n^2h\delta^4\asymp\epsilon^9n^{-7/10},
 \quad
 n^3hH\delta^4\asymp\epsilon^{10},
 \quad
 n^4h^2H\delta^4\asymp\epsilon^{15}n^{-1/2}.
 \tag{36}
\]
Moreover \(nH\delta^2\asymp\epsilon^3n^{1/10}\to\infty\), so \(n^2h\delta^2\leq Cn^3hH\delta^4\) for \(n\geq n_0(\epsilon)\).  Equations (35)--(36) give the remaining inequalities in (25).  This also explains why the divergent fixed-reference fifth projection is absent: the sign-dependent common singleton likelihood (26) is the dominating marginal before the bounded-overlap comparison, rather than a factor expanded around \(P_\star\).
added_lemmas.justification: Conditioning on the macro signs and normalizing by the exact common one-observation marginal bypasses the divergent fixed-reference odd-singleton attachments.
added_lemmas.gap: The calculation is at the mandated rough stress tuple and does not optimize a lower map over all smoothness regimes.

added_lemmas.statement:
For \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), and every fixed \(L\geq2\), there are constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(L\) and the fixed bumps, such that
\[
 \rho_n^*\geq c n^{-3/10}
 \qquad\text{for every }n\geq n_0.
 \tag{33}
\]
Every component of the null prior used for (33) has exactly \(\tau\equiv1/8\), every alternative component belongs to the original binary exact-uniform-design class and has \(D(P)\geq c n^{-3/10}\), and the comparison is in the original fixed-\(n\) experiment.  Consequently, at this tuple,
\[
 c n^{-3/10}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4/19},
 \qquad
 \frac{\rho_n^*}{\rho_{n,e}^*}\geq c n^{1/10},
 \tag{34}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a sufficiently small constant \(\epsilon>0\), put \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), choose the legal integer meshes and amplitudes from \(\texttt{lem:conditional-common-marginal-hellinger}\), and use the full causal laws constructed in \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection-corrected}\).  That lemma verifies, equation by equation, exact uniform design, consistency, conditional exchangeability, the three Hölder restrictions, overlap, both binary-regression margins, and componentwise \(\tau_0\equiv1/8\).  It also gives a constant \(c_0>0\), independent of \(n\), such that every alternative component satisfies
\[
 D(P_1)\geq c_0\delta=c_0\epsilon n^{-3/10}.
 \tag{35}
\]

Let \(\bar P_0^{(n)}\) and \(\bar P_1^{(n)}\) be the two fixed-\(n\) prior-predictive laws.  By (25), after choosing \(\epsilon\) small enough and then \(n_0\) large enough,
\[
 H^2(\bar P_0^{(n)},\bar P_1^{(n)})\leq\frac14.
\]
For the convention in (25), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P,Q)
 =\frac12\int|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)
 \leq H(P,Q),
\]
so the preceding display implies \(\operatorname{TV}(\bar P_0^{(n)},\bar P_1^{(n)})\leq1/2\).

For any measurable randomized test \(\phi\), the variational characterization of total variation, applied to \(0\leq\phi\leq1\), yields
\[
 \mathbb E_{\bar P_0^{(n)}}\phi
 +\mathbb E_{\bar P_1^{(n)}}(1-\phi)
 \geq1-\operatorname{TV}(\bar P_0^{(n)},\bar P_1^{(n)})
 \geq\frac12.
 \tag{36}
\]
If \(\phi\in\Phi_n\), every null-prior component is in \(\mathcal H_0\), so the first expectation in (36) is at most \(a_0=0.05\).  Hence the average alternative type-II error is at least \(0.45>b_0=0.20\).  By (35), this remains true for every requested separation \(\rho\leq c_0\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), since all prior alternatives then belong to \(\mathcal H_1(\rho)\).  The definition of \(\rho_n^*\) proves (33).

At this tuple \(t=\min(1,1/5)=1/5\) and \(d>4t\).  The already proved single-scale upper bound therefore gives exponent
\[
 \frac{4t}{4t+3d}=\frac{4/5}{4/5+3}=\frac4{19},
\]
which proves the upper inequality in (34).  The known-propensity benchmark gives \(\rho_{n,e}^*\leq Cn^{-2/5}\); dividing (33) by that upper bound proves the ratio lower bound in (34).
added_lemmas.justification: This is an original fixed-\(n\), all-test converse on the unchanged exact-uniform binary class, with every null-prior component exactly homogeneous.
added_lemmas.gap: It closes one rough tuple but not the complete smoothness frontier or the matching upper exponent there.
added_lemmas.consumer: The complete-frontier question and the later known-versus-unknown propensity comparison.

added_lemmas.statement:
At \(d=\gamma=1\) and \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), fix nested integer meshes \(h\asymp\delta^5\) and \(H\asymp\delta\).  There is a legal deterministic alternative \(P_\delta\in\mathcal P(1/10,1/10,1,L,1)\), for every sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), with \(D(P_\delta)\asymp\delta\), and a constant \(c=1/8\), such that for every fine bin \(B\),
\[
 g_B(c):=\operatorname{Cov}_{P_\delta}(A,Y\mid X\in B)
          -c\operatorname{Var}_{P_\delta}(A\mid X\in B)=0.
 \tag{37}
\]
Consequently every proposed nested \(2+1\) or cross-fine \(2+2\) population kernel that contains a within-bin factor
\[
 Z_{ij}(c)=\frac{(A_i-A_j)\{Y_i-cA_i-Y_j+cA_j\}}2
\]
and multiplies it only by functions of disjoint observations and deterministic bin labels has expectation zero under \(P_\delta\).  Thus those pair-factor signals do not furnish the deterministic alternative dichotomy needed for a matching \(n^{-3/10}\) upper bound.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let the fine bins be the intervals of length \(h\).  In each bin \(B\), choose a translated and rescaled \(C^\infty\) function \(\psi_B\), compactly supported in the interior of \(B\), with
\[
 \mathbb E_B\psi_B=0,
 \qquad \mathbb E_B\psi_B^2=\mu_\psi>0,
 \qquad \|\psi_B\|_\infty\leq1.
\]
Choose \(H^{-1}\) integral and put \(G_H(x)=\sin(2\pi x/H)\), so \(\int_0^1G_H=0\) and \(\int_0^1G_H^2=1/2\).  Let \(q=k\delta^{1/2}\), where \(k>0\) is fixed, and define
\[
 v_B=-\frac{\delta\,\mathbb E_B G_H}{q\mu_\psi},
 \qquad
 e=\frac12+q\sum_B\psi_B,
\]
\[
 m_0=\frac38+\sum_Bv_B\psi_B-2\delta G_H,
 \qquad
 \tau=\frac18+4\delta G_H.
 \tag{38}
\]
For \(X\in B\), the disjoint supports imply \(e_B=\mathbb E_Be=1/2\).  The exact binned identity gives
\[
 g_B(c)=\operatorname{Cov}_B(e,m_0)+(1-e_B)\mathbb E_B[e(\tau-c)].
\]
For completeness, this identity follows directly from
\[
 \mathbb E_B(AY)=\mathbb E_B\{e(m_0+\tau)\},
 \quad
 \mathbb E_BA=e_B,
 \quad
 \mathbb E_BY=\mathbb E_Bm_0+\mathbb E_B(e\tau),
 \quad
 \operatorname{Var}_B(A)=e_B(1-e_B),
\]
by expanding \(\operatorname{Cov}_B(A,Y)-c\operatorname{Var}_B(A)\) and collecting the \(m_0\) and \(\tau-c\) terms.
Using \(\mathbb E_B\psi_B=0\) in (38), the two terms are
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_B(e,m_0)
 =qv_B\mu_\psi-2q\delta\mathbb E_B(\psi_BG_H),
\]
and
\[
 (1-e_B)\mathbb E_B[e(\tau-c)]
 =\delta\mathbb E_BG_H+2q\delta\mathbb E_B(\psi_BG_H).
\]
Their sum is \(qv_B\mu_\psi+\delta\mathbb E_BG_H=0\) by the definition of \(v_B\), proving (37).

The rescaled bump bounds give \([\sum_B\psi_B]_{1/10}\leq C h^{-1/10}\).  Since \(|v_B|\leq\delta/(q\mu_\psi)=C\delta^{1/2}\), the two fine-scale Hölder seminorms in (38) are bounded by a constant times \(\delta^{1/2}h^{-1/10}\), which is constant when \(h\asymp\delta^5\).  Also \([\delta G_H]_1\leq2\pi\delta/H\), and its \(1/10\)-Hölder seminorm is bounded by a fixed multiple of \(\delta H^{-1/10}\).  By choosing the fixed proportionality constants in \(h\asymp\delta^5\) and \(H\asymp\delta\), and then taking \(\delta\) small, the propensity, baseline, and CATE seminorms are at most \(L\); their supremum norms are at most \(L\) as well.  The perturbations in (38) converge uniformly to zero, so all three pointwise margins hold for sufficiently small \(\delta\).  Construct binary potential outcomes conditionally independently of treatment given \(X\), exactly as in the corrected diagnostic lemma, to obtain consistency, exchangeability, and exact uniform design.  Hence \(P_\delta\) is in the original class.  Finally,
\[
 D(P_\delta)=4\delta\left(\int_0^1G_H^2\right)^{1/2}
 =2\sqrt2\,\delta.
\]

For two iid observations conditioned to lie in the same fine bin, direct symmetrization gives \(\mathbb E[Z_{ij}(c)\mid X_i,X_j\in B]=g_B(c)=0\).  A multiplier depending only on disjoint observations and deterministic bin labels is conditionally independent of \((A_i,Y_i,A_j,Y_j)\) given those labels.  Iterated expectation and (37) therefore make every stated \(2+1\) or \(2+2\) population kernel zero.  Since \(D(P_\delta)>0\), no dichotomy based only on those means can be valid.
added_lemmas.justification: This supplies the exact blind alternative required before claiming a deterministic dichotomy for the proposed pair-factor omnibus upper test.
added_lemmas.gap: It refutes only the stated pair-factor population architecture, not all possible multiresolution tests.
added_lemmas.consumer: The complete-frontier question uses it to isolate the remaining upper-side obstruction.

proposed.name: Pstar
proposed.def: \(P_\star\) has \(X\sim\lambda\) and conditional cell probabilities \((p^\star_{00},p^\star_{01},p^\star_{10},p^\star_{11})=(5/16,3/16,1/4,1/4)\) for \((A,Y)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The retained projection diagnostics take an \(L^2\) norm under this fixed reference, so the reference must be declared rather than left implicit.

The old statement used unit sup-norm synthesis bounds while assuming only a bounded-overlap synthesis constant; the replacement imposes \(C_bq_e\leq1/4\) and \(C_bq_b+2\delta\leq1/8\) and rechecks the class membership.
The fifth-projection diagnostic must inherit the corrected third-projection hypotheses and use the corrected margin implication.

proposed.statement: On the identical class \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), define independently two finite, explicitly evaluable constructions.  The upper construction must select deterministic multiresolution tuning and produce one total data-driven test in \(\Phi_n\), with rejection probability at most \(a_0\) for every \(n\), worst-case type-II error at most \(b_0\) above a displayed upper-radius map, and certified arithmetic and memory costs in every dense and sparse occupancy regime.  The lower construction must consist of realizable full-cube binary laws in the same class, every component of each null prior must have exactly constant \(\tau\), and an original fixed-\(n\) likelihood, Hellinger, or total-variation calculation must give a displayed lower-radius map against all tests.  Neither repaired construction may be defined from the frozen quantities \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) or \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\), which remain regression diagnostics only.  Prove the corresponding upper and lower inequalities for \(\rho_n^*\), optimize both maps for every fixed \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), including every equality-case logarithm, and prove that the independently obtained maps have the same order before introducing any common sharp-rate notation.  If they do not match, give the explicitly evaluable two-sided bracket and isolate the exact unmatched population-signal, stochastic-projection, or prior-predictive connected-cluster term.
proposed.justification: This remains the field-tier theorem target: the new stress-tuple converse is material, but a total uniformly calibrated upper test and independently optimized matching maps are still required on the identical class.
proposed.gap: At the rough stress tuple the direct conditional Hellinger comparison now proves \(\rho_n^*\gtrsim n^{-3/10}\).  The proposed pair-factor \(2+1\)/\(2+2\) upper architecture has an exact legal blind alternative with every fine-bin covariance contrast equal to zero, and the all-regime lower optimization and transition logarithms remain unresolved.
proposed.consumer: A completed theorem would give causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows a genuine detectability benchmark and an omnibus finite-sample procedure, without certifying any fitted forest or converting non-rejection into a homogeneity conclusion.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The dependency spine must retain the corrected projection diagnostics and incorporate the new direct-Hellinger converse and the exact upper-side blind alternative.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a total multiresolution test whose population signal does not vanish on the exact covariance-masking alternative, prove uniform finite-sample level and power with every sparse-occupancy projection, and optimize it; independently extend and optimize the constant-null-supported direct-Hellinger converse over all \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d)\), then compare the maps and determine every boundary logarithm.
open_obligations.obstruction: The lower route now closes at \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), but it has not been optimized outside that tuple.  On the upper side, the explicit legal construction in \(\texttt{prop:pair-factor-omnibus-blind-alternative}\) has \(D(P)\asymp\delta\) while \(g_B(1/8)=0\) in every fine bin.  Therefore both a canonical \(2+1\) kernel and a cross-fine \(2+2\) energy whose population means contain a within-bin pair factor have zero mean, so the required deterministic alternative dichotomy is false for that architecture.
open_obligations.attempted: The bounded-overlap margins were corrected and the class membership was rechecked.  Conditional on the macro signs, the exact common singleton likelihood was used as the dominating marginal.  The published partition-mixture lemma was instantiated with cell masses \(O(h)\), density ratios bounded by the original margins, \(\delta_1,\delta_2=O(\delta)\), and \(\delta_3=0\).  Convexity over the shared outer-sign prior left no extra outer term; the conditional cost \(n^2h\delta^2\) is absorbed at the mandated stress scaling, yielding the fixed-sample \(n^{-3/10}\) converse.  For the upper route, the binned covariance identity was solved exactly for a smooth baseline perturbation that cancels every proposed pair-factor population signal while retaining nonconstant CATE.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The unchanged-class all-regime bracket remains
\[
 c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n,
 \qquad
 b_n=\begin{cases}
 n^{-2t/(4t+d)},&d\leq4t,\\
 n^{-4t/(4t+3d)},&d>4t,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}.
\]
The no-penalty region \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\), \(d\leq4\gamma\), remains matched, with no logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\).  At the rough stress tuple \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), the sign-conditioned common-marginal calculation proves the sharper original-class lower bound
\[
 c n^{-3/10}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4/19},
 \qquad \rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\geq c n^{1/10}.
\]
The conditional partition-mixture calculation leaves \(n^2h\delta^2=O(\epsilon^7n^{-1/10})\), but this is absorbed by \(n^3hH\delta^4=\Theta(\epsilon^{10})\) for fixed \(\epsilon\) and large \(n\); no additional outer-sign term remains after Hellinger convexity.  The fixed-reference fifth projection remains a valid construction diagnostic but is not a Hellinger obstruction after normalization by the common singleton law.  On the upper side, an exact legal alternative with \(D(P)\asymp\delta\) and \(g_B(1/8)=0\) in every fine bin makes the proposed pair-factor \(2+1\) and \(2+2\) population means vanish.  A different omnibus population signal and its sparse-occupancy concentration theory are therefore still required, as are all-regime lower optimization, matching, and transition logarithms.  The frozen \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) remain diagnostics, and no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

prose_updates.tldr: The established all-regime observational bracket and matched no-penalty region remain valid, and the rough stress point now has a sharper original-class converse.  With \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), the general lower bound is \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\) and the explicit upper bound is \(n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), or \(n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\).  At \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), conditioning on macro signs and normalizing by the exact common one-observation law proves \(c n^{-3/10}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4/19}\), hence \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\geq c n^{1/10}\).  The matching upper route remains open because a legal covariance-masking alternative makes all proposed pair-factor \(2+1\) and \(2+2\) population means vanish.  No common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Existing homogeneity tests and adjacent minimax results do not give a fixed-sample sharp radius on this project-specific binary exact-uniform class.  The direct-Hellinger calculation now proves a material \(n^{-3/10}\) lower bound at the canonical rough tuple, but the best proved upper exponent there is \(4/19\), and the complete three-index map and its transition logarithms remain unknown.
project_justification.niche: The live niche is the interaction between a constant-effect composite null, separately rough propensity and baseline functions, exact full-cube design, and collision information beyond binned covariance means.  The sign-dependent common marginal is sufficient for a sharp new converse at one rough tuple, while the exact masking example shows that an attaining test must use an omnibus signal richer than products of within-bin covariance contrasts.
project_justification.fill: The paper currently supplies the explicit total fourth-order test and all-regime bracket, the known-propensity benchmark and no-penalty region, a corrected constant-null-supported nested construction, and a direct fixed-\(n\) Hellinger converse of order \(n^{-3/10}\) at \((1,1,1/10,1/10)\).  It also gives an explicit legal blind alternative that rules out the proposed pair-factor upper dichotomy.  These are field-level advances and precise constraints on the missing matched frontier, not a claim that the frontier is complete.

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 remains a method donor rather than the source of the present class.  Its Theorem 1 concerns pointwise CATE estimation in a larger model, and its binary lower submodel uses a covariate density uniform on a support with holes.  Here only its Section 3.2 partition-mixture Hellinger lemma is instantiated after separately proving exact full-cube cell masses, common predictive marginals, and density-ratio bounds.  NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 supplies collision-sensitive conditional-independence testing on a different null and metric; LundborgKimShahSamworth2024 supplies projected-covariance validity and spline power under its own common-smoothness conditions; DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026 gives asymptotic homogeneity procedures under nuisance conditions; and McGrathMukherjee2026 derives separate resolutions for a signed expected conditional-covariance estimation functional.  None supplies the new constant-null-supported \(n^{-3/10}\) fixed-sample converse or repairs the covariance-masking failure of the proposed upper statistic on this identical class.
prose_updates.interpretation: At the rough stress tuple, unknown assignment is provably consequential: the observational critical radius is at least order \(n^{-3/10}\), whereas supplying the propensity permits order \(n^{-2/5}\), so their ratio diverges at least as \(n^{1/10}\).  This is a detectability statement about worst-case laws, not a guarantee for any fitted forest, and non-rejection cannot be interpreted as evidence of homogeneous effects.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The corrected bounded-overlap construction satisfies the original margins through \(|u|\leq C_bq_e\) and \(|v|\leq C_bq_b\).  Conditional on macro signs, its common singleton likelihood lies between \(11/12\) and \(13/12\) relative to the interior reference.  The localized Hellinger calculation has \(\delta_1,\delta_2=O(\delta)\), \(\delta_3=0\), and cost \(Cn^2h\delta^2\); at \(h\asymp\delta^5\), \(H\asymp\delta\), \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), this is \(O(\epsilon^7n^{-1/10})\) and is eventually absorbed by \(n^3hH\delta^4=\Theta(\epsilon^{10})\).  Hellinger convexity adds no outer-sign term.  The fixed-reference fifth projection still diverges and remains a valid warning against that chi-square normalization, but it is not an obstruction to the common-marginal comparison.  The unresolved obstruction is now upper-side: a legal alternative can have nonconstant CATE and \(g_B(c)=0\) in every fine bin, annihilating the proposed pair-factor population signals.  A richer statistic, all sparse-regime concentration bounds, and all-regime matching are still missing.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The statistical class remains the original binary exact-full-cube-uniform Hölder class with fixed overlap and interior margins; no nuisance-rate or estimator-side condition has been inserted.  The proved global result is still a bracket, augmented by a sharper \(n^{-3/10}\) lower bound and a strict known-versus-unknown separation at one rough tuple.  The no-penalty subregion remains sufficient but not necessary.  The complete frontier, the exact propensity-equality region, and unproved transition logarithms remain open.  The corrected third and fifth projections diagnose one construction, while the masking proposition diagnoses one proposed upper architecture; neither is promoted to a universal impossibility theorem.
